newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BROKER BLASTS STATE OVER BOURSE CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BROKER BLASTS STATE OVER BOURSE CRISIS.

text.p: Athens broker Anastasios Siafakas, vice-president of the Association of Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA), blamed state short-comings for the bourse's recent crisis in an open letter to Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
He questioned why the state National Bank was an intermediary in settlements with the clearing house without ever having signed any pertinent contract.

He also said that despite an abundant legal and regulatory framework the exchange proved unprepared to deal with the recent settlement crisis because the state had been indifferent on implementation of various measures and laws.

"The exchange's guarantee fund was set up to protect investors and not crooks. But the state has for a long time turned a deaf ear to calls to properly staff its supervisory services," Siafakas said in his letter to Simitis. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
